Flow Clone

Everything runs on this PC. Nothing is sent over the network.

Shortcuts

Keys: Ctrl, Win, Alt, Shift, Space, Esc, A–Z, 0–9, F1–F24. Ctrl/Alt/Shift match either side; Left Alt, Right Alt (also Left/Right Ctrl, Shift) match one side only, e.g. push to talk = Right Alt. Max 3 keys, at least one modifier.

Audio
Speech model

Checking…

Whisper: a whisper.cpp ggml model, e.g. ggml-base.bin (default) or ggml-small-q5_1.bin for better accuracy. Parakeet: the sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-int8 folder (needs a build with the parakeet feature). Models are never downloaded automatically: put them in .

Transcription

"comma", "new line", "quote … unquote", "in parentheses", "um", "scratch that", "$5", "3pm" — handled on this PC with or without the AI model. Off = exactly what you said (same as cleanup level Verbatim).

After a paste the field is re-read for about 45 s. Words you fix show up under Dictionary → Suggestions; nothing is added without your OK.

AI cleanup (local LLM)

Off.

Polishes what the formatting rules leave: run-on sentences, leftover fillers, corrections, tone per app. Runs llama.cpp on this PC ( next to the app). Off: the formatting rules still run. Skipped when the text is already clean; if the model is slow or changes too much, the formatted transcript is pasted instead. Loading takes a little longer than before (the instructions are prepared at load).

Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M is the fast default; Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct is more accurate and about twice as slow. Never downloaded automatically.

Cleanup engine
Engine: On-device

On-device = the local model above. OpenRouter = text cleanup in the cloud, off until you turn it on and agree in the OpenRouter tab.

Writing style

Which style applies depends on the app you dictate into. Chats default to casual, email and everything else to formal.

        Speech-to-text (sends audio)

        The order of the engines (server, this PC, OpenRouter) is under Developer → Engines.

        Text cleanup (sends text)

        Sent: the transcript, the app category and writing style, your dictionary words. Not sent unless you turn it on below: text around the cursor, words on screen, the app name.

        Cloud cleanup is used for on-device and cloud dictations. Your server uses its own AI.

        Usage this month

          Shared by speech and cleanup. When the next request could pass it, OpenRouter is skipped until next month.

          Send audio to OpenRouter?

          When on, the audio of your dictations leaves this PC and is sent to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai) and the model provider it routes to, along with your dictionary words. Routed only to zero-retention providers by default.

          You can turn this off at any time.

          Send dictated text to OpenRouter?

          After each dictation, the text (and your dictionary words) is sent to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai) and to the model provider it routes to. Your voice is not sent unless Cloud speech-to-text is also on. Routed only to zero-retention providers by default.

          You can turn this off at any time.

            Engines

            Where speech is turned into text. Client = this PC. Server = your own flow-server (LAN or Tailscale); audio goes only there, never to a third party. OpenRouter = cloud speech-to-text, turned on and set up in the OpenRouter tab; only its place in the order is set here.

            Try in this order (the next one is the fallback):

                Speech decoding

                Transcribes each finished phrase while you keep talking, so a long dictation is ready about as fast as a short one (cuts go in pauses of 0.8 s or more). Off = the whole recording is transcribed after you stop. OpenRouter always gets the whole recording at the end.

                Parakeet only (whisper ignores it). Changing it reloads the model.

                Server

                Stored encrypted for your Windows account (DPAPI); never logged.

                Debug log

                When on, each dictation's raw and final text, timings, engine and target app are written to (last 500) and printed to the console. It stays on this PC and never contains your server token, API keys or clipboard. Turn it off when you are done.
